title: Console: Minimal rollout & simplified trace/cost surface (MVP cuts & acceptance criteria)
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description: This ticket captures the scoped-down implementation plan and acceptance criteria for the Console Observability MVP. After cross-functional review we must reduce surface area to meet the launch date while preserving core value: per-route latency and cost visibility plus a lightweight tracing view to diagnose obvious regressions. The document lists specific cuts, rationale, rollout strategy, monitoring/alerting to watch during canary, and explicit acceptance criteria for QA and sign-off.
decisions: Cut detailed per-token cost breakdown card from MVP; replace with aggregated per-route cost/day metric to reduce query cardinality and backend cost.
Defer span-level trace drilldowns and related UI (deep flamegraphs) to post-MVP; keep a single-pane sampled-traces list with basic metadata (duration, error flag, route).
Ship coarse time-bucketed cost trends (day, week) and hide high-cardinality filters (user_id, session_id) behind a "+filters" gate for enterprise-only future work.
Keep rollout gated by canary on 5% of orgs, with automatic rollback on increased 5xx or >20% increase in query latency compared to baseline.
Favor server-side rollups and cached aggregates over live per-request joins to meet latency SLOs for dashboard queries.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard landing (top-level cards) loads < 600ms P90 in canary; < 1s P90 for public rollout.
Per-route aggregated cost card returns within 800ms P95 and matches billing export within ±10% for sample orgs.
Sampled traces list can be queried for time-range and route; selecting a trace returns raw span payload within 1s for 90% of requests.
No new high-cardinality queries on backend (DB slow query list shows zero occurrences of filters on user_id/session_id in canary period).
Canary rollout telemetry: alert if console-route-query-5xx rate increases by >50% or dashboard-p90-latency increases by >30% vs baseline for 15m.
UX: New cards have tooltip explanations and a first-time run onboarding panel; PM/Design sign-off on copy and layout before full rollout.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Removing per-token cost detail could confuse customers used to fine-grained billing analysis. Mitigation: add a short modal explaining deferred features and a contact link to Sales for enterprise reporting.
Risk: Sampling rate too low causing undiagnosable incidents. Mitigation: start with 5% sampling for canary orgs and allow manual increase for debugging windows via internal admin tool.
Risk: Aggregation errors cause cost mismatch. Mitigation: run reconciliation job against billing exports for sample orgs during canary and hold rollout if mismatch >10%.
Risk: Backend query load spikes. Mitigation: enable query throttling and fast-fail with user-facing "Data delayed" state; circuit-break to cached aggregates.
rollout_plan: Day 0: Deploy UI behind feature flag and enable server-side rollups. Canary enable for 5% of orgs (random sampling by org id).
Day 1-3: Monitor telemetry (dashboard-latency, route-query-5xx, billing-recon mismatch). Daily sync with infra & SRE.
Day 4: If no major alerts and billing recon <10%, expand to 25% orgs. Continue running reconciliation job nightly.
Day 7: Public rollout if stability and recon thresholds met; otherwise iterate on slow queries and aggregation logic.
Rollback criteria: any sustained >50% increase in 5xx or >30% P90 latency deterioration for 15 minutes triggers automatic rollback to previous console build.
qa_checklist: Smoke test: dashboard loads with test org seeded data (small/medium/large) within latency targets.
Billing reconciliation: night-run job reconciles per-route aggregated cost against billing export for 3 sample orgs.
Tracing sanity: sample traces show correct route mapping and include span count and error flag.
Feature-flag flows: ensure UI hidden for orgs without flag; admin can toggle canary state.
Accessibility: top-level cards keyboard navigable and ARIA labels present.
